perspective:
From Ethan’s available perspective:

- I am Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is my close, long-time friend from middle school; he is a doctor. We have often relied on each other for emotional and professional support.
- I noticed Gary working extremely long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. I became concerned and invited him to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- Gary initially told me he appreciated my concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, I observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work.
- I suspected there was more to his overworking than just professional obligations. I confronted him, saying he could tell me anything and that I was there to help, not judge.
- Gary told me, “It’s complicated,” and that he didn’t want to burden me with his problems. He then opened up about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- I suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, I regularly checked in with Gary. He told me things were better, that my help made him less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie last weekend. I told him I was proud and available to talk.
- After a year, I saw Gary managing better/on his own. I felt satisfied and happy for him and decided to step back. I told him I was always a call away and knew he had this. Gary thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and felt more in control.
